A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpatialCrafter and have readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting comparison. v1 includes Appendices A-D; the supplied v2 ends after the references. This omission can be assessed alongside the retained material.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation and scene-reconstruction experiments, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1-6, ablations, and additional qualitative experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1-6 and associated qualitative comparisons and ablations, and includes additional reconstruction visualizations in Figure 7.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces Depth Pro/COLMAP point-cloud scale alignment with VGGT geometry estimation and Metric3D depth alignment using an inter-percentile-range ratio. VGGT also replaces DUSt3R for input-camera inference. This substantially revises the central pose/scale-calibration component, while retaining the camera conditioning, epipolar attention, and Mamba-Transformer reconstruction architecture.

E1.justification: The named training and benchmark datasets and principal generation/reconstruction tasks remain unchanged. Explicit supplementary scenario coverage contracts: v2 omits the prescribed roll, translation, and zoom demonstrations and progressive single-view exploration examples in v1's Appendix C and Figures 10-13. v2 Figure 7 remains within previously represented indoor, outdoor, and synthetic domains.

E2.justification: v2 removes the comparison against Kling and Gen-3 Turbo in v1 Section 4.4/Figure 9. Comparator membership in Tables 1-6 and the retained qualitative comparisons is unchanged; newly cited methods such as CameraCtrl II and Gen3C are not added to those evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 reports revised camera-pose preprocessing for joint-dataset training through VGGT/Metric3D rescaling. The shared experimental sections retain their budgets, resolutions, sampling settings, and metrics. v1's appendix conflicts with its main text on batch size and evaluation pose estimation; deleting those appendix statements does not establish doubled resources, a changed evaluator, or rerun experiments.

E4.justification: v2 removes the commercial-model camera-transition analysis, controlled motion/amplitude demonstrations, and progressive-exploration case study from v1 Section 4.4 and Appendix C. These withdrawals substantially reduce supplementary analysis of controllability and reconstruction completeness. The principal component ablations remain unchanged: Table 6 and v1 Figures 7-8 survive as v2 Table 6 and Figures 8-9.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests for the experimental results. Error metrics and shot-transition percentages are performance measurements, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All method entries and numerical values in Tables 1-6 are identical. v2 removes v1 Figure 9's shot-transition rates of 29% for Gen-3 Turbo, 23% for Kling, and 11% for SpatialCrafter, together with numerous appendix qualitative outcomes. Figure 7 adds indoor reconstruction examples and 3DGS displays, partly revisiting scenes already illustrated in v1; no quantitative performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 introduces an explicit scale definition, s = IPR(dv)/IPR(dm), using the 0.8 and 0.2 percentiles, and the transformation Pscaled = [R|sT]. v1 instead describes point-cloud alignment without this rule. The retained epipolar mathematics and denoising/reconstruction objectives are substantively unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: video priors alleviate sparse-view ambiguity, scale alignment enables multi-dataset training, and depth/latent fusion supports Gaussian reconstruction. The revised calibration implementation and withdrawn supporting experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 omits Appendix D's explicit limitations concerning inference cost and insufficient user interaction; restricted frame coverage remains discussed in Section 3.2. It also removes substantive explanations in Appendices B-C and Section 4.4 concerning robustness to geometric-estimation failures, progressive completion through exploration, and smoother camera transitions. The paper consequently provides substantially less qualification and interpretation.

D1.justification: Removing Appendix A eliminates unique details about trainable modules, noise scheduling, center cropping, frame intervals of 2-10, dataset sequencing, 256-by-256 evaluation, and RoMa overlap estimation with its 0.005 threshold. v2 supplies more explicit calibration instructions and adds a project-page URL, but these additions do not replace the substantial lost reproduction information.

R1.justification: v2 adds CameraCtrl II, Wonderland, Gen3C, VideoScene, VGGT, Metric3D, NVS-Solver, and FLARE, while removing Depth Pro. Section 2 more explicitly acknowledges video-prior reconstruction approaches. However, Appendix B.1's detailed distinctions from ViewCrafter, DimensionX, ReconX, and CAT3D disappear, substantially contracting the comparative positioning despite the updated citations.

P1.justification: The dominant structural revision is removal of Section 4.4 and the entire appendix organization covering implementation, discussion, qualitative results, and limitations. v2 also compresses introductory and related-work prose, rewrites scale alignment, and changes author/affiliation information. Much of the remaining main text and its section order is preserved.

P2.justification: Figures 1-2 are redesigned, with Figure 2 adding a system overview and epipolar-attention inset. v2 introduces the Figure 7 video/3DGS montage, removes the commercial-model comparison and appendix figure suite, and rearranges displays such as Table 5. The existing ablation figures are retained and renumbered, rather than replaced by new analyses.

improvement.justification: v2 benefits from clearer pipeline graphics, updated research positioning, and more explicit calibration instructions. However, it loses unique evaluation and training details, targeted supplementary analyses, and explicit cost/interaction limitations, reducing reproducibility and critical appraisal. v1's appendix contains some conflicting settings, but its deletion also removes useful information without replacement. The principal comparisons and core claims remain intact, so the evidence supports a limited overall decline rather than a collapse of the experimental case.
